title: The Contact of Kowloon
premise: Lior Quintana, a veteran hostage negotiator haunted by the one call she failed twenty years ago in Kowloon, receives a debt notice from a stranger claiming she owes a favor she never received — a favor that was actually taken out in her name by the covert program that trained her. As she traces the ledger of manufactured obligations, she realizes the network has been using negotiators like her as deniable assets for decades, and that her old mentor is its architect. Hunted by former colleagues who are also on the books, Lior must decide whether loyalty to the people who made her outweighs the truth of what they made her do. In the end she burns the program's central archive during a staged negotiation gone live, exposes the ledger publicly, and walks away with her name finally her own — though the last entry in the book is written in her handwriting.
about_author: Marguerite Montrose is the pen name of a former crisis-line counselor who spent eleven years listening to strangers talk their way out of corners. She writes thrillers about people whose professional calm conceals private fault lines.

chapters.title: The Favor
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A courier delivers an elegant card: 'Favor returned, with interest owed,' referencing a debt from Kowloon, 2004 — a negotiation Lior never ran. She checks the archives and finds her signature on documents she never signed. Emotional beat: the floor tilts; her ordered life becomes evidence of something she can't name.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Following the paper trail to a defunct shipping firm, she finds a ledger of favors logged against dozens of negotiators — herself listed forty-one times. Her old mentor, Edmund Voss, denies everything too smoothly. Beat: dread hardens into purpose; she stops asking whether and starts asking who.

chapters.title: The Stranger Who Owes Nothing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Lior and the stranger, Tomas Reyes, a former program asset who sent the card to force exposure before the network erases him. He shows her how favors were converted into operational leverage. Beat: wary alliance; two liars learning each other's tells over bad coffee.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The network retaliates: her current negotiation caseload is manipulated so a live standoff turns lethal, framing her judgment. Internal affairs suspends her. Beat: humiliation and clarity — they aren't punishing her, they're demonstrating what obedience buys.

chapters.title: Kowloon, Again
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Lior's POV. Twenty years earlier: the real failed negotiation, the hostage who died, and Voss quietly rewriting the record — inserting himself as the hero, her as the failure, and logging the 'favor' that saved her career. Beat: grief reframed; her defining wound was authored.

chapters.title: The Quiet Ones
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. He gathers other ledger names — retired negotiators living careful, small lives — and finds some would rather protect the network than face what they did. One betrays them. Beat: betrayal within the alliance; loyalty revealed as the network's true currency.

chapters.title: Interest Accrued
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. With Reyes missing, presumed taken, Lior plays debtor: she approaches Voss offering silence in exchange for the archive key, negotiating exactly as she was trained — using his own rules against him. Beat: cold exhilaration; the student out-negotiating the teacher, and knowing he knows.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The handoff at a container terminal collapses into a staged hostage scenario — the network's masterpiece, using Reyes as the hostage and Lior as the sanctioned negotiator. Beat: rising terror; every move pre-scripted except the ones she improvises.

chapters.title: Burn Rate
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, climax. Mid-standoff, she flips the script: broadcasts the ledger to press, police, and every named asset simultaneously, making the archive worthless and the network's secrecy fatal. Voss, exposed mid-lie, loses control of his own negotiation. Beat: cathartic fury; truth deployed like a weapon.

chapters.title: Settled Accounts
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, resolution. Investigations begin; assets come forward or vanish; Voss awaits trial, still convinced he taught her everything. Lior visits the Kowloon memorial, leaves no flowers, signs nothing. Final beat: quiet freedom — and one last envelope, in her own handwriting, she doesn't remember writing.
